hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.

paper.title: Cholesterol dysregulation in APOE4 astrocytes promotes α-synuclein pathology in miBrains.

findings.finding_description: Lysosomal proteolytic capacity was measured with the self-quenched substrate DQ-BSA in isogenic APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 iPSC-derived astrocytes. APOE4/4 astrocytes showed significantly lower lysosomal DQ-BSA signal in both isogenic donor pairs (Donor #2: p < 0.0001). Lipid metabolism was not measured or manipulated in this experiment.
findings.quote: APOE4/4 astrocytes showed significantly reduced lysosomal DQ-BSA signal compared to isogenic control APOE3/3 astrocytes across two isogenic donor pairs (Donor #1: p= 0.0032; Donor #2: p < 0.0001, Figure 4d), indicating decreased lysosomal proteolytic activity.
findings.summary: APOE4/4 human iPSC astrocytes have reduced lysosomal proteolysis (DQ-BSA) compared with isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes, in two donor pairs.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (2D monoculture), two donor pairs

findings.finding_description: DQ-BSA fluorescence was normalized to co-internalized, protease-resistant dextran to separate lysosome number from per-organelle function. APOE4/4 astrocytes still showed significantly lower proteolytic activity than APOE3/3 astrocytes, indicating a functional lysosomal deficit rather than only reduced lysosome abundance.
findings.quote: Even after dextran normalization, APOE4/4 astrocytes retained significantly lower proteolytic activity (p = 0.0098; Figure S4e), indicating functional impairment rather than solely reduced lysosome abundance.
findings.summary: The lysosomal proteolysis deficit in APOE4/4 astrocytes persists after normalizing for lysosomal loading (dextran).
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (2D monoculture)

findings.finding_description: Immunoreactivity for the lysosomal membrane protein LAMP1 was significantly reduced in APOE4/4 versus isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes in two donors (Donor #2: p = 0.0001). LAMP1 serves as a surrogate for lysosomal mass rather than lysosomal function.
findings.quote: immunoreactivity for the lysosomal membrane protein LAMP1 was also significantly reduced in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared to isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes (Donor #1: p = 0.0002 and Donor #2: p = 0.0001, Figure S4d)
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes have less LAMP1 (lysosomal mass marker) than APOE3/3 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (2D monoculture), two donor pairs

findings.finding_description: Astrocytes were loaded with fluorescent α-Syn-HiLyte for 24 h, then extracellular α-Syn was removed and the intracellular signal was tracked for 24 h. APOE3/3 astrocytes cleared the signal significantly (p < 0.0001); APOE4/4 astrocytes showed no significant decrease (p = 0.694). This is a surrogate for lysosomal degradation, given that clearance was bafilomycin-sensitive.
findings.quote: APOE3/3 astrocytes showed a significant reduction in intracellular α-Syn-HiLyte signal (p < 0.0001), whereas APOE4/4 astrocytes showed no significant decrease (p = 0.694; Figure 4c), indicating impaired degradation of α-Syn.
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes fail to degrade internalized α-Syn, whereas APOE3/3 astrocytes clear it.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes, live imaging

findings.finding_description: Uptake of exogenous α-Syn-HiLyte was monitored by live imaging. APOE4/4 astrocytes showed delayed uptake, with no increase at 4.5 h (p = 0.9997) and only a modest increase at 6 h (p = 0.0006). APOE3/3 astrocytes showed significant accumulation by 4.5 h. This is an endocytic-pathway surrogate.
findings.quote: isogenic APOE4/4 astrocytes showed delayed uptake, with no detectable increase of α-Syn at 4.5 hours (p = 0.9997) and only a modest increase by 6 hours (p = 0.0006)
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes show delayed endocytic uptake of α-Syn compared with APOE3/3 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes, live imaging

findings.finding_description: Immunoblotting showed increased total and phosphorylated α-Syn protein in APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 astrocytes across two donors, despite lower SNCA mRNA. This is consistent with post-translational, possibly degradative, impairment, but it is an indirect surrogate for lysosomal function.
findings.quote: immunoblotting of astrocyte monocultures revealed increased total and phosphorylated α-Syn protein in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared with isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes across two donors (Total α-Syn: Donor #1: p = 0.023; Donor #2: p= 0.043
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes accumulate α-Syn protein despite reduced SNCA transcript.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (monoculture), two donors

findings.finding_description: Astrocytes treated with bafilomycin A1 showed blocked α-Syn-HiLyte degradation (p = 0.0241), whereas MG-132 had no significant effect (p = 0.079). This validates the degradation assay as a lysosomal readout. Class 5 because neither APOE genotype nor lipid metabolism was varied; it only supports the surrogate B'.
findings.quote: Lysosomal inhibition significantly blocked the degradation of α-Syn-HiLyte (p = 0.0241), whereas proteasomal inhibition had no significant effect (p = 0.079; Figure S4c)
findings.summary: Astrocytic α-Syn clearance is lysosome-dependent, not proteasome-dependent.
findings.experimental_system: human iPSC-derived astrocytes

findings.finding_description: snRNA-seq GSEA of APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 astrocytes in miBrains showed altered lipid droplet biogenesis gene sets (P = 0.04). This bears on APOE4 disrupting lipid metabolism, but no lysosomal endpoint was measured. Class 5 because it addresses only the lipid side of the mechanism, through a transcriptional surrogate.
findings.quote: GSEA of astrocytes showed altered expression of genes associated with inflammatory states (P = 0.03), matrisome (P = 0.0004), α-Syn pathology (P = 0.04), and lipid droplets biogenesis (P = 0.04) in APOE4/4 astrocytes
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes in miBrains show transcriptional changes in lipid droplet biogenesis genes.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 iPSC-derived miBrains, astrocyte snRNA-seq

findings.finding_description: In a screen of cholesterol-reducing small molecules in APOE4/4 astrocytes, 2HβCD and MβCD significantly increased DQ-BSA lysosomal proteolysis. Here cholesterol lowering is a surrogate perturbation of the lipid-metabolism arm, and lysosomal function is measured directly.
findings.quote: Treatment with 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (2HβCD) and methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD) significantly increased lysosomal proteolysis (2HβCD: p = 0.0002; MβCD: p = 0.019) (Figure 5b)
findings.summary: Cyclodextrin cholesterol extraction rescues lysosomal proteolysis in APOE4/4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with cyclodextrins

findings.finding_description: The other small molecules that reduce cholesterol bioavailability did not improve lysosomal proteolysis in APOE4/4 astrocytes; their effects were neutral or negative. This partly argues against a general cholesterol-lowering mechanism.
findings.quote: whereas the other interventions had neutral or negative effects on APOE4/4 lysosomal proteolytic activity (Figure 5b)
findings.summary: Non-cyclodextrin cholesterol-lowering agents failed to rescue APOE4 lysosomal proteolysis.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with cholesterol-reducing small molecules

findings.finding_description: The MβCD-induced increase in DQ-BSA lysosomal proteolysis in APOE4/4 astrocytes was replicated in astrocytes from a second donor.
findings.quote: Increased lysosomal proteolytic activity with MβCD was replicated in astrocytes from a second donor (p = 0.0045; Figure S5c).
findings.summary: Cyclodextrin rescue of APOE4 lysosomal proteolysis replicates across donors.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes, second donor

findings.finding_description: APOE4/4 astrocytes showed increased BODIPY-cholesterol accumulation versus isogenic APOE3/3 in two donors. Class 5 because this measures the lipid-metabolism intermediate of the hypothesis (the APOE4-to-lipid link), not the lysosomal outcome.
findings.quote: APOE4/4 astrocytes showed significantly increased BODIPY-cholesterol accumulation compared to isogenic APOE3/3 astrocytes generated from two different individuals (Donor #1: p = 0.001; Donor #2: p = 0.002, Figure 5a).
findings.summary: APOE4/4 astrocytes accumulate cholesterol versus APOE3/3.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes (2 donors)

findings.finding_description: Filipin staining showed increased free cholesterol in APOE4/4 versus APOE3/3 astrocytes, which MβCD reduced to APOE3/3-comparable levels. Class 5 because this measures the lipid intermediate (and validates the surrogate), not lysosomal function.
findings.quote: Filipin staining revealed a significant increase in endogenous free cholesterol in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared to APOE3/3 astrocytes, which was significantly reduced following MβCD treatment (p = 0.0167) to levels comparable to APOE3/3 astrocytes (Figure S5b).
findings.summary: APOE4 astrocytes have elevated free cholesterol, normalized by MβCD.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes ± MβCD

findings.finding_description: Cyclodextrins decreased BODIPY-stained neutral lipids in APOE4/4 astrocytes to APOE3/3-like levels. Class 5 because this verifies that the surrogate perturbation changes lipid content, without measuring the lysosomal outcome.
findings.quote: Treatment with cyclodextrins significantly decreased neutral lipids in APOE4/4 astrocytes as measured by BODIPY staining (2HβCD: p = 0.0013; MβCD: p = 0.0063) to levels comparable to APOE3/3 astrocytes (Figure 5c).
findings.summary: Cyclodextrins normalize neutral lipid levels in APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes ± cyclodextrins

findings.finding_description: MβCD increased LysoTracker-positive lysosomal signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes, with similar effects for both cyclodextrins in another donor. LysoTracker is an acidic-compartment surrogate for lysosomal function, and cyclodextrin is a surrogate input.
findings.quote: Consistent with improved lysosomal capacity, MβCD increased LysoTracker-positive lysosomal signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.044; Figure 5d), with similar effects observed across donors (2HβCD: p < 0.0001; MβCD: p < 0.0001, Figure S5d).
findings.summary: Cholesterol extraction increases LysoTracker signal in APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes ± cyclodextrins

findings.finding_description: After 4 h incubation, the fraction of α-Syn-HiLyte co-localizing with LysoTracker was lower in APOE4/4 than in APOE3/3 astrocytes. This is a surrogate for endolysosomal delivery and handling.
findings.quote: the percentage of α-Syn-HiLyte that co-localized with LysoTracker decreased in APOE4/4 astrocytes compared to APOE3/3 (p = 0.0395; Figure S5f)
findings.summary: Less α-Syn reaches lysosomes in APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes

findings.finding_description: MβCD increased α-Syn-HiLyte/LysoTracker colocalization in APOE4/4 astrocytes, bringing it to levels not different from vehicle-treated APOE3/3.
findings.quote: APOE4/4 astrocytes treated with MβCD showed increased colocalization of α-Syn-HiLyte with LysoTracker compared to vehicle-treated APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.0343).
findings.summary: Cholesterol extraction restores lysosomal delivery of α-Syn in APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes ± MβCD

findings.finding_description: Cyclodextrin-treated APOE4/4 astrocytes showed increased 24-h uptake of α-Syn-HiLyte, replicated in a second donor. Endocytic uptake is a surrogate for endolysosomal function.
findings.quote: Cyclodextrin-treated APOE4/4 astrocytes showed significantly increased uptake of α-Syn-HiLyte at 24 hours (2HβCD: p = 0.0009; MβCD: p = 0.0001) compared to vehicle-treated APOE4/4 astrocytes (Figure 5e).
findings.summary: Cholesterol extraction increases α-Syn uptake by APOE4 astrocytes.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 human iPSC-derived astrocytes ± cyclodextrins

findings.finding_description: Bulk transcriptomics of APOE4/4 astrocytes showed differential expression of genes involved in lipid storage and transport. Class 5 because this is a transcriptional correlate of the lipid arm only, with no lysosomal measure.
findings.quote: transcriptomic analysis of APOE4/4 astrocytes showed differential expression of genes (p < 0.05) involved in lipid storage and transport, as well as response to lipopolysaccharide and oxidative stress
findings.summary: APOE4 astrocytes have altered lipid storage/transport gene expression.
findings.experimental_system: isogenic APOE4/4 vs APOE3/3 human iPSC-derived astrocytes

findings.finding_description: 7-day MβCD treatment reduced neuronal phosphorylated α-Syn in APOE4/4 miBrains to levels not different from APOE3/3. Class 5 because the readout is downstream neuronal pathology, not lysosomal function.
findings.quote: the levels of neuronal phosphorylated α-Syn were significantly reduced in MβCD-treated APOE4/4 miBrains (p = 0.0172) when compared to untreated APOE4/4 miBrains
findings.summary: Cholesterol extraction reduces neuronal p-Syn in APOE4 miBrains.
findings.experimental_system: APOE4/4 iPSC-derived multicellular miBrains with SNCA-A53T neurons
